sources.title: Ember-1 API & Playground
sources.evidence: Exact Ember-1 page lists 2.78T parameters, MoE, image input and function calling; context is displayed as 1040k. Its September 22 date is creation metadata.

sources.title: Introducing Ember-1
sources.evidence: September 23, 2026 launch says available today, identifies Fireworks Research and the Ember series, and describes a Kimi K3 derivative trained for shorter reasoning. Release is a hosted research preview.

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway live model metadata
sources.evidence: The exact fireworks/ember-1 object reports context_window 1048576, text/image input, text output, reasoning and tool-use tags. JSON was retrieved directly and saved under /tmp/model-audit-186/vercel-models.json.

sources.title: Ember-1 (Fireworks) - Cloudflare AI documentation
sources.evidence: Cloudflare documents 1,040,000 context tokens, text generation and function calling for Ember-1, and links to Fireworks terms. This differs from the Vercel route metadata.

sources.title: Fireworks Terms of Service, July 10, 2026
sources.evidence: The official link redirects to a PDF, retrieved with curl and extracted with pdftotext after the web tool failed. Sections 2 and 7 limit service access and reserve Fireworks ownership; no open-weight license is granted.

sources.title: Kimi K3 on Fireworks: Fast RL at frontier scale
sources.evidence: October 12, 2026 systems report was retrieved directly after web-tool failure. Its 2.8T hybrid MoE and layer/expert table explicitly describe Kimi K3, not Ember-1; no Ember-specific active count is supplied.

sources.title: Can open models carry readable silent signals before they speak?
sources.evidence: August 12, 2026 interpretability report was retrieved directly. It studies Kimi K3 and Qwen3.5-9B; it does not establish additional Ember-1 architecture or parameter specifications.

sources.title: LAB leaderboard by Harvey - Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index
sources.evidence: October 20, 2026 first-party comparison distinguishes Fireworks Ember-1 from Moonshot Kimi K3. It provides evaluations and serving methodology, not an Ember active-parameter count.

sources.title: Ember-1 API, Pricing & Playground
sources.evidence: Official serving-provider page identifies the Ember-1 research preview, image input, function calling, Fireworks legal terms and September 23 release date.

name.note: Exact public model name and endpoint match the assigned record.

developer.note: Fireworks identifies this as its own model, developed by Fireworks Research.

family.note: Normalized label for the explicitly named Ember model series; Kimi K3 is the underlying model, not the product family.

release_date.note: The dated launch explicitly announces availability that day. September 22 on the model page is labeled Created on and does not establish public release. Later gateway listings are not the first release.

open_weights.note: The documented release provides hosted research-preview access under Fireworks terms. No public Ember-1 checkpoint or weight-download license was identified in the official release, model page or targeted first-party/Hugging Face searches; base-model openness does not establish derivative availability.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted access under Fireworks commercial service terms, not an SPDX weight license. No open license for the Ember-1 derivative is documented.

parameters_b.note: The exact model page reports 2.78T: 2,780 billion parameters. Treat as a nominal vendor figure, not a tensor-exact count.

active_parameters_b.note: Reviewed exact-model documentation, later first-party training research and comparison tables do not publish Ember-1 active parameters. Third-party 104B figures inherit Kimi K3 specifications; no exact-Ember primary confirmation was found, so that count is not transferred.

architecture.note: The Ember page explicitly confirms mixture-of-experts. More specific hybrid-attention structure is documented for Kimi K3; it is not asserted for this unreleased checkpoint.

context_window.note: Use the developer-published nominal 1040k limit, represented as 1040000 tokens and corroborated by Cloudflare. Vercel reports 1048576 for its route; this provider difference remains documented rather than replacing the developer limit. No endpoint execution was tested.

modalities.note: Vercel explicitly enumerates these modalities for the exact model; the developer independently confirms image input.

reasoning.note: The release discusses reasoning traces and the live provider metadata exposes reasoning controls.

tool_call.note: Developer lists function calling as supported; exact provider metadata includes tools and tool_choice.

description.value: Fireworks reasoning model based on Kimi K3, trained to shorten reasoning traces for coding and agentic tasks.
description.note: Replaces the unqualified quality claim with a concise purpose and lineage description. Approximately 40% fewer tokens at comparable quality is a developer-reported evaluation result, not a universal performance guarantee.

patch.description: Fireworks reasoning model based on Kimi K3, trained to shorten reasoning traces for coding and agentic tasks.
patch.notes: 2.78T is the vendor-reported total; Ember-1 active parameters are undisclosed. Context follows Fireworks’ advertised 1040k tokens (1,040,000), also documented by Cloudflare; Vercel lists 1,048,576 for its route.

sources.label: Vercel AI Gateway live model metadata

summary: Adds the directly disclosed nominal 2,780B total and MoE architecture, Ember family and proprietary service classification. Corrects public release to September 23 and shortens the description. Active parameters remain undisclosed. Uses the developer-advertised 1,040,000 context while documenting Vercel’s 1,048,576 route metadata.
